 For Respondent(s) :
 UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following  O R D E R 1. Exemption Application is allowed.
2. The petitioner  herein is an aged lady and happens to be the mother-in-law of the deceased.

She has been put to trial with other co-accused for the offence punishable under Sections 304B, 498A,
323, 504, 506 and 316 of the Indian Penal Code (for short `IPC) and Sections 3 and 4 respectively of the Dowry Prohibition Act.
3. She prayed for bail before the High Court and the High Court has denied the same.

sentences.text:
Reason:
4. In such circumstances, the petitioner is here before this Court with the present petition.
5.
The learned counsel appearing for the petitioner vehemently submitted that her client is in jail as an under-trial prisoner past 4 years.
Till this date, the prosecution has been able to examine only 2 witnesses.
He further pointed out that the prosecution intends to examine as many as 27 witnesses.
6. It has been the consistent stand of this Court that if the trial has commenced and the prosecution witnesses are being examined, the Court should remain loath in considering the plea of bail.
At the same time, what has been pointed out by the learned counsel also should not be ignored.
If it has been almost 4 years since the petitioner was arrested and the trial court has been able to examine only 2 witnesses out of 27 witnesses, then definitely it is a matter of concern 7.

In such circumstances, referred to above, we direct the Trial Court that if need be, the prosecution witnesses be examined on day-to-day basis and complete the trial within a period of 6 months from today with judgment.
8. This Court has repeatedly reminded the Trial Courts that do not multiply the witnesses.
It is a futile exercise to call multiple witnesses only to establish one particular factum.
9. It is the quality of the evidence that is important and not the quantity of the evidence.
10. With the aforesaid, the Special Leave Petition stands disposed of.
11. Pending applications, if any, also st(and disposed of.
(VISHAL ANAND) (POOJA SHARMA)
